records.source: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστηκότων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐληλυθυῖαν ἐν δυνάμει.
records.gloss: And he was saying to them, Truly I say to you that there are some of those here standing who no not shall taste of death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power.
pieces: He went on to say to them, "Truly I tell you, some who stand here will not taste death until the kingdom of God has come in power and they have seen it."

L.1: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power."

R.1: Then Jesus told them, "I tell you the truth: some people standing here will not die until they see the kingdom of God come with power."

decisions.choice: the kingdom come with power: most likely what the three disciples see on the mountain six days later (9:2-8), a first view of the kingdom in power
alternatives: Jesus' resurrection and the coming of the Spirit
the final coming of the Son of Man in 8:38
decisions.reason: Mark sets this saying directly before the transfiguration and ties the two together with "after six days" (9:2). Only "some" will see it, and only three disciples go up the mountain. Others read the saying as pointing to the resurrection and what followed it, or to the final coming spoken of in 8:38. The text does not settle the question.

decisions.choice: taste death: die
decisions.reason: To taste death is a way of saying to experience death, to die.

decisions.choice: will not: a double negative, a strong denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make a firm promise: they will certainly not die first.

decisions.choice: having come: a perfect participle, the kingdom seen as already arrived
decisions.reason: They will see the kingdom as something that has come and is present in power.

decisions.choice: he was saying to them: the saying closes the teaching of 8:34-38
alternatives: the start of a new scene
decisions.reason: The chapter break comes in the middle of a speech. Jesus is still speaking to the crowd and the disciples of 8:34.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as at 3:28. Readable says "not die" for the idiom "taste death".

records.source: Καὶ μετὰ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν μόνους.
records.gloss: And after days six takes along Jesus Peter and James and John, and brings up them into a mountain high, apart, alone.
pieces: Six days later Jesus took Peter, James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and led them up a high mountain, away from everyone else.

L.2: And after six days Jesus takes along Peter and James and John and brings them up onto a high mountain, apart, by themselves.

R.2: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they climbed a high mountain. Only the four of them were there.

decisions.choice: takes along, brings up: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: he took them and led them up.

decisions.choice: after six days: counted from the sayings of 8:27-9:1; it may also recall Moses on Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Mark rarely gives exact times. In Exodus 24:15-16 the cloud covered Sinai for six days before God called Moses out of the cloud. With the cloud and the voice in 9:7, the echo may be intended.

decisions.choice: a high mountain: Mark does not name it
decisions.reason: Later tradition named Mount Tabor in Galilee. Mount Hermon lies near Caesarea Philippi, where the last scene took place (8:27). Mark leaves it unnamed.

decisions.choice: apart, alone: privately, just the four of them
decisions.reason: Two phrases together stress that no one else was there, as in 4:34 and 6:31.

decisions.choice: Only the four of them were there
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who was on the mountain.

records.heading: Transfigured on the mountain

records.source: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο στίλβοντα λευκὰ λίαν οἷα γναφεὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐ δύναται οὕτως λευκᾶναι.
records.gloss: And he was transfigured before them, \v 3 and the garments of him became shining, white exceedingly, such as a launderer on the earth not is able thus to whiten.
pieces: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured in front of them.
His clothes turned dazzling and intensely white, white beyond what any launderer on earth could achieve.

L.3: and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments became shining, exceedingly white, such as no launderer on earth is able to whiten [them].

R.2: There, while they watched, Jesus' appearance was changed.
R.3: His clothes began to shine. They became whiter than anyone on earth could ever wash them.

decisions.choice: transfigured: his form was changed so that a heavenly glory showed
alternatives: he only looked different in the light
decisions.reason: The verb means to change form. Paul uses it of believers being changed into the Lord's likeness (2 Corinthians 3:18). Mark describes only the clothes, but the change is in Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: was transfigured: a passive, God is the one who changed him
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action.

decisions.choice: launderer: a fuller, who cleaned and bleached new wool and cloth
decisions.reason: Fullers whitened cloth with lye and fuller's earth. Even their best work could not match this whiteness.

decisions.choice: shining white clothes: the clothing of heaven
decisions.reason: White clothing marks God and heavenly beings (Daniel 7:9; Mark 16:5).

decisions.choice: transfigured
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the word long used for this event. Readable says what it means: his appearance was changed.

records.source: καὶ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Ἠλίας σὺν Μωϋσεῖ, καὶ ἦσαν συλλαλοῦντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: And appeared to them Elijah with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
pieces: Then Elijah appeared to them along with Moses, and the two were talking with Jesus.

L.4: And Elijah with Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.

R.4: Then the disciples saw Elijah and Moses there. These two great men from long ago were talking with Jesus.

decisions.choice: Elijah and Moses: the great prophet and the giver of the law
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:4-5 names Moses and Elijah together at the close of the prophets. Both met God on a mountain (Exodus 24; 1 Kings 19:8), and neither had an ordinary burial (Deuteronomy 34:6; 2 Kings 2:11).

decisions.choice: Elijah with Moses: Elijah is named first
decisions.reason: Mark names Elijah first. Elijah's coming is what the disciples ask about on the way down (9:11-13).

decisions.choice: appeared: they were seen, a word used of heavenly appearances
decisions.reason: The word means was seen. It is used of appearances from God, such as the risen Jesus (1 Corinthians 15:5).

decisions.choice: the disciples saw; these two great men from long ago
decisions.reason: Readable names who saw them and says who Elijah and Moses were.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Ῥαββί, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
records.gloss: And answering Peter says to Jesus, Rabbi, good it is for us here to be, and let us make three tents, for you one and for Moses one and for Elijah one.
pieces: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, "Rabbi, how good it is that we are here! Let us set up three shelters, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah."

L.5: And Peter responds and says to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tents, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah."

R.5: Peter said to Jesus, "Teacher, this is a good place for us to be. We will make three shelters. One will be for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, another for Moses, and a third for Elijah."

decisions.choice: answering: speaking up, though no question was asked
decisions.reason: The word often simply introduces what someone says in response to a situation.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a Hebrew title of respect, my master, used for a teacher
decisions.reason: The title means my great one. It was used for teachers of the law and is the first time Mark uses it for Jesus.

decisions.choice: tents: shelters, such as huts of branches
decisions.reason: The word means a tent or booth. Peter seems to want to keep the moment and the visitors there.

decisions.choice: tents: perhaps recalling the Festival of Booths or the tent where God met Moses
decisions.reason: Israel lived in shelters at the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:42-43), and God spoke with Moses in a tent (Exodus 33:7-11). Mark does not say what Peter had in mind.

decisions.choice: one for you, one for Moses, one for Elijah: Peter puts the three side by side
decisions.reason: Peter treats the three as equals. The voice from the cloud corrects this (9:7).

decisions.choice: shelters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word for a simple temporary structure. Readable also says "Teacher" for the Hebrew title Rabbi.

records.source: οὐ γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἀποκριθῇ, ἔκφοβοι γὰρ ἐγένοντο.
records.gloss: Not for he knew what he should answer, terrified for they became.
pieces: He did not know what to say, because they were all badly frightened.

L.6: For he did not know what he should answer, for they had become terrified.

R.6: Peter did not know what to say, because the three of them were very afraid.

decisions.choice: for ... for: Mark explains Peter's words
decisions.reason: Mark gives two reasons: Peter did not know what to say, and they were terrified. His offer came from fear and confusion.

decisions.choice: terrified: overcome with fear
decisions.reason: The word is a strong one, used of Moses trembling at Sinai (Hebrews 12:21).

decisions.choice: answer: respond, say
decisions.reason: As in 9:5, the verb means to speak in response to what was happening.

decisions.choice: Peter; the three of them
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant.

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο νεφέλη ἐπισκιάζουσα αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And there came a cloud overshadowing them, and there came a voice out of the cloud, This is the Son of me, the beloved; listen to him.
pieces: Then a cloud came and cast its shadow over them, and a voice spoke from the cloud: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.7: And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved; listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.7: Then a cloud came and covered them with its shadow. A voice came from the cloud and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: the cloud: the cloud of God's presence
decisions.reason: God came down in a cloud on Sinai and filled the tent of meeting with a cloud (Exodus 24:15-18; 40:34-35). The voice comes from the cloud, so the speaker is God.

decisions.choice: This is my Son, the beloved; listen to him: the words of 1:11 again, and the prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: The voice repeats what was said at Jesus' baptism (1:11; Psalm 2:7). "Listen to him" recalls Deuteronomy 18:15, where Moses says God will raise up a prophet like him, and Israel must listen to him.

decisions.choice: This is: the voice now speaks to the disciples about Jesus
decisions.reason: At the baptism the voice said "You are" to Jesus. Here it tells the three who he is and what they must do.

decisions.choice: overshadowing them: covering with its shadow, perhaps all on the mountain
decisions.reason: "Them" may mean Jesus with Moses and Elijah, or the disciples too. Mark does not make it clear.

decisions.choice: my dearly loved Son (B); my Son, and I love him (R)
decisions.reason: The same renderings as at 1:11.

records.source: καὶ ἐξάπινα περιβλεψάμενοι οὐκέτι οὐδένα εἶδον ἀλλὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν.
records.gloss: And suddenly having looked around, no longer no one they saw except Jesus alone with themselves.
pieces: All at once they looked around and saw no one there with them any more, only Jesus.

L.8: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.

R.8: Suddenly the disciples looked around. Moses and Elijah were gone. Only Jesus was there with them.

decisions.choice: no longer ... no one: a double negative for emphasis
decisions.reason: The negatives strengthen each other: there was no one at all except Jesus.

decisions.choice: Jesus alone: the one they were told to listen to remains
decisions.reason: After the voice says "listen to him", Moses and Elijah are gone, and Jesus is left with them.

decisions.choice: Moses and Elijah were gone
decisions.reason: Readable says who had disappeared.

records.source: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ ἃ εἶδον διηγήσωνται, εἰ μὴ ὅταν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ.
records.gloss: And descending of them from the mountain he instructed them that to no one what they had seen they should tell, except when the Son of Man out from [the] dead had risen.
pieces: As they came down the mountain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them orders not to describe what they had seen to anyone until the Son of Man rose from the dead.

L.9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructed them to tell no one what they had seen, except when the Son of Man had risen from [the] dead.

R.9: On the way down the mountain, Jesus ordered them to keep what they had seen to themselves. They were to tell no one until the Son of Man had come back to life from death.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this title for himself, as in 8:31 and 8:38. It recalls the one like a son of man in Daniel 7:13-14.

decisions.choice: except when: the silence lasts only until the resurrection
decisions.reason: This is the only command to silence in Mark with a time limit. After the resurrection the event could be understood and told.

decisions.choice: risen from the dead: raised to life again
decisions.reason: The phrase means coming back to bodily life, as Jesus said in 8:31.

decisions.choice: They were to keep quiet until
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence in two and states the time limit plainly.

records.heading: Elijah has come

records.source: καὶ τὸν λόγον ἐκράτησαν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς συζητοῦντες τί ἐστιν τὸ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.
records.gloss: And that saying they kept to themselves, questioning what is the out from [the] dead to rise.
pieces: They kept the matter to themselves, but they debated with one another what this "rising from the dead" might mean.

L.10: And they kept the word to themselves, questioning what the rising from [the] dead is.

R.10: So they did not tell anyone. But they talked with each other about what Jesus meant by "rising from the dead."

decisions.choice: to themselves: goes with kept, they told no one
alternatives: goes with questioning: they discussed it among themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase can belong with either verb. With "kept" it says they obeyed the order of 9:9; with "questioning" it says they discussed it among themselves. Both are true in the scene.

decisions.choice: the word: the saying, the command and what it said about rising
decisions.reason: The noun often means a matter or saying as a whole, as in 8:32.

decisions.choice: what rising from the dead is: they could not see how the Son of Man could rise before the end
alternatives: they did not believe in resurrection
decisions.reason: Many Jews expected all the righteous to rise together at the end of the age (Daniel 12:2). The disciples did not understand a single person rising first.

decisions.choice: what Jesus meant by
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that they were puzzling over Jesus' words.

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ὅτι λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
records.gloss: And they were asking him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elijah it behooves to come first?
pieces: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do the scribes claim that Elijah has to come first?"

L.11: And they were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"

R.11: Then they asked Jesus, "Why do the teachers of God's law say that Elijah must come first?"

decisions.choice: why: the small word here opens a question
alternatives: that: introducing a statement, the scribes say that
decisions.reason: The word usually means "that", but at the head of a question it can mean "why", as in 9:28.

decisions.choice: Elijah must come first: the promise of Malachi 4:5-6
alternatives: a saying of the scribes only
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the Lord. The scribes taught that he would come first, before the Messiah.

decisions.choice: first: before the end, and before the Messiah
alternatives: before the Son of Man rises
decisions.reason: The disciples have just seen Elijah and heard Jesus speak of his own death and rising. They ask how this fits the order the scribes taught.

decisions.choice: the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Readable says who the scribes were.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἠλίας μὲν ἐλθὼν πρῶτον ἀποκαθιστάνει πάντα, καὶ πῶς γέγραπται ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἵνα πολλὰ πάθῃ καὶ ἐξουδενηθῇ;
records.gloss: And he was saying to them, Elijah indeed having come first restores all things; and how has it been written of the Son of Man that many things he should suffer and be set at naught?
pieces: He told them, "Elijah does come first and set everything right. Then why does Scripture say that the Son of Man is to suffer much and be scorned?

L.12: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things; and how is it written of the Son of Man that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?

R.12: Jesus answered, "It is true that Elijah comes first and makes everything right again. But then why do the Scriptures say that the Son of Man will suffer a great deal, and that people will treat {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as worthless?

decisions.choice: indeed: Jesus grants the scribes' point
decisions.reason: The small word agrees with the statement before the next clause adds a "but".

decisions.choice: restores all things: puts all things back in right order
alternatives: brings the world to an end
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:6 says Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers.

decisions.choice: it is written: Scripture speaks of the suffering of the Son of Man
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name the passage. Isaiah 53:3 and Psalm 22 speak of one who is despised and suffers. Mark gives no single text.

decisions.choice: how: a question that sets two teachings side by side
decisions.reason: If Elijah sets everything right, why must the Son of Man suffer? Jesus' answer in 9:13 is that Elijah has come and was himself mistreated.

decisions.choice: be treated with contempt: be counted as nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as worthless. It is a different word from the one used for being rejected in 8:31.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Readable names what is written.

records.source: ἀλλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ Ἠλίας ἐλήλυθεν, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἤθελον, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐπ’ αὐτόν.
records.gloss: But I say to you that also Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they desired, as it has been written of him.
pieces: But I tell you that Elijah has in fact come, and they did to him as they pleased, just as it is written about him."

L.13: But I say to you that Elijah also has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him."

R.13: But I tell you, Elijah has already come. And people did whatever they wanted to him, just as the Scriptures say about him."

decisions.choice: Elijah has come: John the Baptizer
decisions.reason: Mark does not name him here, but he has shown John dressed like Elijah (1:6; 2 Kings 1:8) and told how Herod killed him (6:17-29). Matthew 17:13 says the disciples understood he meant John.

decisions.choice: as it is written of him: what Scripture says of Elijah
alternatives: a prophecy of John by name
decisions.reason: Scripture tells how Jezebel sought Elijah's life (1 Kings 19:2, 10). What happened to John matches what Elijah suffered.

decisions.choice: they did: those who opposed him, Herod and Herodias in John's case
decisions.reason: The subject is not named.

decisions.choice: already; people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Elijah's coming is past and names the subject in general terms.

records.source: Καὶ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εἶδον ὄχλον πολὺν περὶ αὐτοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς συζητοῦντας πρὸς αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And having come to the disciples they saw a crowd great around them, and scribes arguing with them.
pieces: When they got back to the other disciples, they found a large crowd surrounding them, and some scribes disputing with them.

L.14: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.

R.14: When Jesus and the three came back to the other disciples, they saw a big crowd around them. Some teachers of God's law were arguing with them.

decisions.choice: having come, they saw: plural, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have the singular, making Jesus the one who saw. The SBLGNT reads the plural, which includes the three disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the others who had stayed below
decisions.reason: Jesus had taken only three up the mountain.

decisions.choice: arguing: disputing
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 9:10 and 8:11. Here it is a dispute, likely over the disciples' failure (9:18).

decisions.choice: the other disciples (B, R); Jesus and the three (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which disciples are meant.

records.heading: I believe; help my unbelief

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐξεθαμβήθησαν, καὶ προστρέχοντες ἠσπάζοντο αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And immediately all the crowd, having seen him, were greatly amazed, and running to [him] were greeting him.
pieces: As soon as the people saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the whole crowd was overcome with wonder, and they ran up to greet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.15: And immediately all the crowd, when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, were greatly amazed, and running up, they greeted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.15: As soon as the people saw Jesus, they were very surprised. They all ran to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to welcome {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: greatly amazed: overcome with astonishment
decisions.reason: Mark uses this strong word only here and at 14:33 and 16:5-6.

decisions.choice: why they were amazed: Mark does not say
decisions.reason: Some suggest Jesus' face still showed the glory of the mountain, as Moses' face shone after Sinai (Exodus 34:29-30). Mark gives no reason; it may simply be his sudden arrival at the right moment.

decisions.choice: all the crowd ... having seen: plural forms with a singular crowd
decisions.reason: The crowd is thought of as many people, so the participles are plural.

decisions.choice: as soon as
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Literal says "immediately" and the other levels vary the phrase.

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς· Τί συζητεῖτε πρὸς αὑτούς;
records.gloss: And he asked them, What are you disputing with them?
pieces: He asked them, "What are you arguing with them about?"

L.16: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What are you disputing with them?"

R.16: Jesus asked them, "What are you arguing with them about?"

decisions.choice: them ... with them: Jesus asks the disciples what they are disputing with the scribes
alternatives: what are you disputing among yourselves
decisions.reason: The pronouns are not explained. Since the scribes were arguing with the disciples (9:14), Jesus most likely asks his disciples. Some manuscripts read the second pronoun as "among yourselves".

decisions.choice: disputing: the same verb as arguing in 9:14
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the word Mark used for the scene.

decisions.choice: What are you arguing with them about?
alternatives: What are you disputing with them?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday verb and English word order.

records.source: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου· Διδάσκαλε, ἤνεγκα τὸν υἱόν μου πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντα πνεῦμα ἄλαλον·
records.gloss: And answered him one out of the crowd, Teacher, I brought the son of me to you, having a spirit mute;
pieces: A man in the crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I brought my son to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.

L.17: And one of the crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, I brought my son to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, [because he] has a mute spirit;

R.17: A man in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought my son to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He has an evil spirit in him that keeps him from talking.

decisions.choice: a mute spirit: a spirit that keeps him from speaking
alternatives: a spirit that does not speak
decisions.reason: The spirit is named by what it does to the boy. In 9:25 it is also called deaf.

decisions.choice: I brought my son to you: he came looking for Jesus
alternatives: he brought him to the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus was on the mountain, so the father asked the disciples instead (9:18).

decisions.choice: one of the crowd: the man is not named
decisions.reason: He is simply a man in the crowd, a father (9:21).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable uses "evil spirit", as in earlier chapters, and says what the spirit does.

records.source: καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν αὐτὸν καταλάβῃ ῥήσσει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀφρίζει καὶ τρίζει τοὺς ὀδόντας καὶ ξηραίνεται· καὶ εἶπα τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου ἵνα αὐτὸ ἐκβάλωσιν, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν.
records.gloss: and whenever if him it seizes, it throws down him, and he foams and gnashes the teeth and is withering; and I spoke to the disciples of you that it they might cast out, and not they had power.
pieces: Whenever it takes hold of him, it dashes him to the ground, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and goes stiff. I asked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to throw it out, but they did not have the strength."

L.18: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds [his] teeth and becomes rigid; and I told {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples to cast it out, and they were not able."

R.18: Whenever the spirit takes control of him, it throws him to the ground. Foam comes out of his mouth, he grinds his teeth, and his body becomes stiff. I asked {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers to force the spirit out, but they could not do it."

decisions.choice: becomes rigid: goes stiff during the attack
decisions.reason: The verb means to dry up or wither. In this list of what happens in an attack it most likely means the body goes stiff. It could mean he is wasting away.

decisions.choice: the attacks: like what is now called an epileptic seizure
decisions.reason: The signs are those of a seizure. Mark tells it as the work of a spirit, and Jesus deals with it as one (9:25). Matthew 17:15 also describes the boy's fits.

decisions.choice: wherever: at any place and time
decisions.reason: The word means where, but with "if" it covers every occasion.

decisions.choice: they were not able: they lacked the strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to have strength. The disciples had driven out spirits before (6:13) but failed here.

decisions.choice: foams at the mouth (B); foam comes out of his mouth (R)
decisions.reason: English needs "mouth" with this verb.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος, ἕως πότε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔσομαι;
records.gloss: And answering them he says, O generation unbelieving, until when with you will I be?
pieces: Jesus answered them, "You unbelieving generation! How long must I stay with you?

L.19: And answering them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you?

R.19: Jesus said to them, "You people do not believe! How long do I have to stay with you?

decisions.choice: them: the whole company, disciples, father, crowd and scribes
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to all of them. The word "generation" takes in the people of his time, the disciples included, since they failed (9:18).

decisions.choice: unbelieving generation: Israel's lack of faith in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 32:5 and 32:20 speak of a crooked generation, children without faithfulness. As Moses came down Sinai to find unfaithfulness (Exodus 32), Jesus comes down to find unbelief.

decisions.choice: unbelieving: without trust in God
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of believing. It points ahead to the father's words in 9:24.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Another of Mark's vivid presents. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: You people do not believe!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the address into a plain statement.

records.source: ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: Until when will I bear with you?
pieces: How long must I bear with you?

L.19: How long will I put up with you?

R.19: How long must I be patient with you?

decisions.choice: until when: how long
decisions.reason: A plain question of time, spoken in sorrow.

decisions.choice: bear with: put up with, endure patiently
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold up under something hard.

decisions.choice: be patient with
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase.

records.source: φέρετε αὐτὸν πρός με.
records.gloss: Bring him to me.
pieces: Bring the boy to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: bring: a plural command, said to those standing there
decisions.reason: The command is plural. In 9:20 several people bring the boy.

decisions.choice: the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the son so the pronoun is not taken for Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ἤνεγκαν αὐτὸν πρὸς αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And they brought him to him.
pieces: So they brought the boy to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.20: So they brought the boy to Jesus.

decisions.choice: him to him: the boy to Jesus
decisions.reason: The first pronoun is the boy, the second Jesus.

decisions.choice: the boy (B, R); Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

records.source: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα εὐθὺς συνεσπάραξεν αὐτόν, καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκυλίετο ἀφρίζων.
records.gloss: And having seen him, the spirit immediately threw into convulsions him, and having fallen on the ground he was rolling around, foaming.
pieces: As soon as the spirit saw Jesus, it threw the boy into a fit. He fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.

L.20: And when the spirit saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, it immediately threw him into convulsions, and falling on the ground, he rolled around, foaming.

R.20: When the evil spirit saw Jesus, right away it made the boy shake violently. The boy fell on the ground. He rolled around, and foam came out of his mouth.

decisions.choice: having seen him: the spirit saw Jesus
decisions.reason: The participle is masculine though "spirit" is neuter. It is joined to the spirit by sense, as a person. It could be read of the boy, but the spirit is the subject of the main verb.

decisions.choice: threw into convulsions: shook him violently
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear or shake about. It describes the seizure.

decisions.choice: was rolling around: went on rolling about
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes continuing movement.

decisions.choice: Jesus; the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant by each pronoun.

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ· Πόσος χρόνος ἐστὶν ὡς τοῦτο γέγονεν αὐτῷ;
records.gloss: And he asked the father of him, How long a time is it that this has been with him?
pieces: Jesus asked the boy's father, "Since when has this been happening to him?"

L.21: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked his father, "How long a time is it since this has happened to him?"

R.21: Jesus asked the boy's father, "When did this start happening to your son?"

decisions.choice: his father: the boy's father
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the boy.

decisions.choice: this: the attacks
decisions.reason: Jesus asks how long the boy has suffered.

decisions.choice: the boy's father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whose father is meant.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐκ παιδιόθεν·
records.gloss: And he said, From childhood;
pieces: He answered, "Since he was a small child.

R.21: The father said, "Since he was a little boy.

decisions.choice: from childhood: since he was very young
decisions.reason: The word points to early childhood. The boy is still a child (9:24).

decisions.choice: The father
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: καὶ πολλάκις καὶ εἰς πῦρ αὐτὸν ἔβαλεν καὶ εἰς ὕδατα ἵνα ἀπολέσῃ αὐτόν· ἀλλ’ εἴ τι δύνῃ, βοήθησον ἡμῖν σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς.
records.gloss: and often both into fire him it cast and into waters, that it might destroy him; but if anything you are able, help us, having compassion on us.
pieces: Many times it has thrown him into fire or into water to kill him. But if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to do anything at all, help us. Have pity on us!"

L.22: and often it has thrown him both into fire and into water, to destroy him; but if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able [to do] anything, help us, having compassion on us."

R.22: The spirit has often thrown him into fire or into water to try to kill him. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything, please feel sorry for us and help us!"

decisions.choice: has thrown: the spirit has done this again and again
decisions.reason: "Often" shows that the past tense sums up many attacks.

decisions.choice: if you are able: the father is not sure Jesus can help
decisions.reason: After the disciples failed, the father doubts. Jesus takes up these words in 9:23.

decisions.choice: having compassion: deep pity
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of feeling stirred within. Mark uses it of Jesus himself (1:41; 6:34; 8:2).

decisions.choice: us: the father counts himself with his son
decisions.reason: The father shares his son's suffering and asks for both of them.

decisions.choice: the spirit; to try to
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and shows that the spirit's aim had not succeeded.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τὸ Εἰ δύνῃ, πάντα δυνατὰ τῷ πιστεύοντι.
records.gloss: And Jesus said to him, The If you are able! All things are possible to the [one] believing.
pieces: Jesus said to him, "'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can!' All things are possible for the one who believes."

L.23: And Jesus said to him, "'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able!' All things [are] possible for the one who believes."

R.23: Jesus said to him, "Why do you say, 'If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can'? Everything is possible for a person who believes."

decisions.choice: 'If you are able!': Jesus repeats the father's words and throws them back
alternatives: Jesus asks if he himself is able
decisions.reason: The article points to the father's phrase as a quotation. The question is not whether Jesus is able but whether the father will trust.

decisions.choice: 'If you are able!', the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: If you are able to believe, all things are possible
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "to believe", which smooths the grammar and makes it a condition placed on the father. The shorter reading is found in the earliest manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one who believes: the father, who answers in 9:24
alternatives: Jesus himself, whose trust in God makes all things possible
decisions.reason: The father replies "I believe", so he takes the words to mean him. Some see Jesus' own trust in God in them too. The two are not exclusive.

decisions.choice: believes: trusts God and his power at work in Jesus
decisions.reason: Believing in Mark is trust that God will act (5:36; 11:22-24).

decisions.choice: Why do you say
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Jesus is quoting the father.

records.source: εὐθὺς κράξας ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ παιδίου ἔλεγεν· Πιστεύω· βοήθει μου τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ.
records.gloss: Immediately having cried out the father of the child was saying, I believe; help of me the unbelief.
pieces: At once the boy's father cried out, "I believe! Help my unbelief!"

L.24: Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, "I believe; help my unbelief!"

R.24: Right away the boy's father shouted, "I do believe! Help me with my unbelief!"

decisions.choice: cried out, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "with tears" and address Jesus as "Lord". The earliest manuscripts lack both. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: help my unbelief: help me where my faith falls short
decisions.reason: The father admits that his trust is mixed with doubt and asks Jesus to help him in that weakness.

decisions.choice: believe, unbelief: the same word family as 9:19 and 9:23
decisions.reason: Believing and unbelief are set side by side in one man.

decisions.choice: Help me with my unbelief
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the father asks help for himself.

records.source: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐπισυντρέχει ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ λέγων αὐτῷ· Τὸ ἄλαλον καὶ κωφὸν πνεῦμα, ἐγὼ ἐπιτάσσω σοι, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηκέτι εἰσέλθῃς εἰς αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Having seen now Jesus that was running together a crowd, he rebuked the spirit, the unclean, saying to it, Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and no more may you enter into him.
pieces: When Jesus saw that a crowd was quickly gathering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the unclean spirit a stern order: "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you to come out of him and never go into him again!"

L.25: Now when Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again."

R.25: Jesus saw that more people were running over to see. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke sternly to the evil spirit. "You spirit that makes this boy deaf and unable to speak," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I order you to come out of him! Never go back into him again!"

decisions.choice: a crowd was running together: more people were gathering
decisions.reason: The word suggests people running up to join. Jesus acts before a larger crowd forms.

decisions.choice: rebuked: commanded sternly
decisions.reason: The same verb Jesus uses with spirits and with the storm (1:25; 4:39).

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, I myself command you
decisions.reason: Jesus stresses his own authority, where the disciples had failed.

decisions.choice: never enter him again: the cure is permanent
decisions.reason: The command shuts the spirit out for good, since its attacks had come and gone (9:18).

decisions.choice: You spirit that makes this boy deaf and unable to speak
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spirit's name means.

records.source: καὶ κράξας καὶ πολλὰ σπαράξας ἐξῆλθεν· καὶ ἐγένετο ὡσεὶ νεκρὸς ὥστε τοὺς πολλοὺς λέγειν ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.
records.gloss: And having cried out and much having convulsed [him], it came out; and he became as if dead, so that the many said that he died.
pieces: The spirit shrieked, threw him into violent convulsions, and came out. The boy was left lying like a corpse, so that most of them said, "He has died."

L.26: And after crying out and convulsing [him] greatly, it came out; and he became like [one] dead, so that the many said, "He has died."

R.26: The spirit screamed and shook the boy hard. Then it came out of him. The boy looked as if he were dead, and many people said, "He is dead."

decisions.choice: having cried out, having convulsed: the spirit is the subject
decisions.reason: The participles are masculine, as in 9:20, but they go with the spirit that comes out.

decisions.choice: the many: most of those there
decisions.reason: With the article the phrase means the majority.

decisions.choice: crying out: a shriek without words
decisions.reason: The spirit had made the boy mute, and no words are reported.

decisions.choice: like a corpse
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a vivid phrase for the boy's lifeless look.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ἤγειρεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀνέστη.
records.gloss: But Jesus having taken the hand of him raised him, and he arose.
pieces: But Jesus took hold of his hand and lifted him up, and he got to his feet.

L.27: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he arose.

R.27: But Jesus took the boy by the hand and helped him up. And the boy stood up.

decisions.choice: raised, arose: the verbs used for resurrection
decisions.reason: The same verbs describe rising from the dead (5:41-42; 9:9-10). The boy seemed dead, and Jesus raises him.

decisions.choice: but: in contrast to those who said he was dead
decisions.reason: The small word sets Jesus' act against the crowd's verdict.

decisions.choice: lifted him up, got to his feet (B); helped him up, stood up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words. Literal keeps the words that recall resurrection.

records.source: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς οἶκον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν· Ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
records.gloss: And having entered he into a house, the disciples of him in private were asking him, Why we not were able to cast out it?
pieces: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went indoors, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, "Why could we not throw it out?"

L.28: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had gone into a house, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"

R.28: Later Jesus went into a house. When {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were alone with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they asked, "Why could we not force the spirit out?"

decisions.choice: why: the small word opens a question
alternatives: that: we could not cast it out
decisions.reason: As in 9:11, the word introduces a question here.

decisions.choice: we: emphatic, we ourselves
decisions.reason: They had driven out demons before (6:13) and are puzzled that they failed.

decisions.choice: a house: a place for private teaching
decisions.reason: Mark often has Jesus explain things to the disciples alone in a house (7:17; 10:10).

decisions.choice: throw out (B); force out (R)
decisions.reason: The same pattern as in earlier chapters.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ.
records.gloss: And he said to them, This kind by nothing is able to go out except by prayer.
pieces: He told them, "This kind cannot be made to come out by any means except prayer."

L.29: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "This kind is not able to come out by anything except by prayer."

R.29: Jesus answered, "Only prayer can make this kind of spirit come out."

decisions.choice: by prayer, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and fasting". The earliest manuscripts lack it. The addition may reflect the growing practice of fasting in the church. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: this kind: this kind of spirit
decisions.reason: Jesus means the kind of spirit that held the boy.

decisions.choice: by prayer: by depending on God
alternatives: by a special prayer said over the boy
decisions.reason: Jesus does not pray aloud in the story. He speaks of the trust in God that prayer expresses, which the disciples lacked (9:19). The words do not explain why this kind needs it more than others.

decisions.choice: this kind of spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind is meant.

records.source: Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντες παρεπορεύοντο διὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἵνα τις γνοῖ·
records.gloss: And from there having gone out they were passing through Galilee, and not did he want that anyone should know;
pieces: They left that place and made their way through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,

L.30: And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not want anyone to know [it];

R.30: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers left that area and traveled through Galilee. Jesus did not want people to know where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was,

decisions.choice: passing through: traveling through without stopping to teach the crowds
decisions.reason: The verb means to go along through a place. The journey now leads toward Jerusalem (10:1, 10:32).

decisions.choice: he did not want anyone to know: because he was teaching the disciples
decisions.reason: The next sentence gives the reason: this was a time to teach the Twelve.

decisions.choice: where they were (B); where he was (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Jesus did not want known.

records.heading: Handed over, killed, and raised

records.source: ἐδίδασκεν γὰρ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀποκτανθεὶς μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.
records.gloss: he was teaching for the disciples of him and he was saying to them that, The Son of Man is handed over into [the] hands of men, and they will kill him, and having been killed after three days he will arise.
pieces: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was busy teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. "The Son of Man is going to be handed over into human hands," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them. "They will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and three days after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is killed {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise again."

L.31: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is handed over into [the] hands of {{gender:people|men}}, and they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been killed, after three days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise."

R.31: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He said to them, "The Son of Man will be handed over to people who will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But three days after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dies, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come back to life."

decisions.choice: is handed over: a present tense for something certain and already under way
alternatives: it is happening at this moment
decisions.reason: The present makes the future sure. The verbs that follow are future.

decisions.choice: handed over: delivered up to others
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Judas handing Jesus over (3:19; 14:10) and of God giving up his servant (Isaiah 53:6 in the Greek). Here the one who hands him over is not named.

decisions.choice: after three days: on the third day
decisions.reason: As in 8:31, the phrase counts parts of days. Mark tells of the rising early on the third day (16:1-2).

decisions.choice: Son of Man ... hands of men: a play on the word for human beings
decisions.reason: The one called the Son of Man is given into the hands of human beings.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels say "handed over", since Jesus does not yet speak of Judas and the verb is wider than betrayal.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι.
records.gloss: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid him to ask.
pieces: But they did not grasp what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant, and they were afraid to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.32: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.32: But the disciples did not understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant, and they were too afraid to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: did not understand, were afraid: imperfects, a lasting state
decisions.reason: They went on not understanding and went on being afraid.

decisions.choice: afraid to ask: perhaps afraid of the answer, or of a rebuke like Peter's (8:33)
decisions.reason: Mark does not say why. The last time a disciple questioned this teaching, Jesus rebuked him.

decisions.choice: what he meant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they did not understand.

records.source: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
records.gloss: And they came to Capernaum.
pieces: They arrived at Capernaum.

R.33: Then they came to the town of Capernaum.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: Jesus' base by the lake
decisions.reason: Jesus had made his home there (1:21; 2:1).

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says what Capernaum was.

records.heading: Who is the greatest?

records.source: καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ γενόμενος ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Τί ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ διελογίζεσθε;
records.gloss: And in the house having been, he was asking them, What on the way were you discussing?
pieces: Once they were inside the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What was it you were debating as we walked?"

L.33: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What were you discussing on the way?"

R.33: When they were inside the house, Jesus asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "What were you talking about while we were walking?"

decisions.choice: the house: a house known to the reader, perhaps Peter's
decisions.reason: The article points to a known house. Simon's house in Capernaum appears in 1:29 and perhaps 2:1.

decisions.choice: discussing: reasoning together, debating
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 8:16-17. The next sentence shows what the debate was.

decisions.choice: the way: the road they traveled
decisions.reason: The word means road. Mark often places teaching "on the way" to Jerusalem (8:27; 10:32).

decisions.choice: What was it you were debating as we walked? (B); while we were walking (R)
alternatives: What were you discussing on the way?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "on the way" into a clause.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων, πρὸς ἀλλήλους γὰρ διελέχθησαν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τίς μείζων.
records.gloss: But they were silent; with one another for they had been discussing on the road who [was] greater.
pieces: They said nothing, because on the way they had been debating among themselves which of them was the greatest.

L.34: But they were silent, for on the road they had been discussing with one another who [was] the greatest.

R.34: But they did not answer. They had been arguing with each other on the road about which one of them was the most important.

decisions.choice: greater: the form meaning greater, used here for greatest
decisions.reason: Greek of this time often used the form for "greater" to mean the greatest of a group.

decisions.choice: who: which one of them
decisions.reason: They were comparing themselves with each other.

decisions.choice: they were silent: they kept quiet out of shame
decisions.reason: Their silence follows Jesus' teaching about his death (9:31).

decisions.choice: the most important
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase for greatness in rank.

records.source: καὶ καθίσας ἐφώνησεν τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἴ τις θέλει πρῶτος εἶναι ἔσται πάντων ἔσχατος καὶ πάντων διάκονος.
records.gloss: And having sat down he called the twelve and says to them, If anyone desires first to be, he will be of all last and of all servant.
pieces: He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them, "Whoever wants to be first must be last of everyone and the servant of everyone."

L.35: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and called the twelve and says to them, "If anyone wants to be first, {{gender:they|he}} will be last of all and servant of all."

R.35: Jesus sat down and called the Twelve to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "If you want to be the most important, you must put yourself last. You must serve everyone else."

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Teachers sat to teach (4:1). The words that follow are formal teaching.

decisions.choice: he will be: a future that works as a command
alternatives: a warning that he will end up last
decisions.reason: The future can state what must be. It could also mean that whoever seeks first place will be put last.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves others, as at table
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a servant who waits on others. Mark uses the word for slave in 10:44.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again.

decisions.choice: If you want to be the most important, you must put yourself last
alternatives: If anyone desires to be first
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearer directly and says what "first" means.

records.source: καὶ λαβὼν παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὸ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς·
records.gloss: And having taken a child he set it in [the] midst of them, and having taken in arms it he said to them,
pieces: He took a little child and stood the child among them. Then, putting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms around the child, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,

L.36: And taking a child, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set it in the middle of them, and taking it in [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] arms, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them,

R.36: Then Jesus took a little child and had the child stand in front of them. He took the child in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arms and said to them,

decisions.choice: a child: someone with no rank or importance
decisions.reason: Children had no standing in that society. Jesus answers the debate about greatness by setting one in the middle.

decisions.choice: taking in his arms: embracing
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold in the arms. Mark uses it again in 10:16.

decisions.choice: it: the word for child is neuter
decisions.reason: Mark does not say whether the child was a boy or a girl.

decisions.choice: the child
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid calling a child "it".

records.source: Ὃς ἂν ἓν τῶν τοιούτων παιδίων δέξηται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται· καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐμὲ δέχηται, οὐκ ἐμὲ δέχεται ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
records.gloss: Whoever one of such little children shall receive in the name of me, me receives; and whoever me shall receive, not me receives but the [One] having sent me.
pieces: "Whoever welcomes a child like this one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And whoever welcomes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is welcoming, not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but the One who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.37: "Whoever receives one of such children in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and whoever receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives not {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} but the One who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.37: "When someone welcomes a little child like this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when they welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are not only welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are also welcoming God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: in my name: for my sake, because the child belongs to me
alternatives: using my name as a formula
decisions.reason: To do something in someone's name is to do it on their account.

decisions.choice: not me but the one who sent me: not only me but also God
alternatives: they do not receive Jesus at all
decisions.reason: "Not this but that" is a common way of putting stress on the second item. Receiving Jesus is receiving God.

decisions.choice: receive: welcome as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb is used for showing hospitality (6:11).

decisions.choice: the One who sent me: God
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as sent by the Father, as in 12:6.

decisions.choice: for my sake; not only ... also; God
alternatives: in my name; not me but the One who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idioms and names God as the sender.

records.source: Ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Διδάσκαλε, εἴδομέν τινα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ἐκωλύομεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠκολούθει ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: Said to him John, Teacher, we saw someone in the name of you casting out demons, and we were forbidding him, because not he was following us.
pieces: John said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we saw a man throwing out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We tried to stop him, since he did not go around with us."

L.38: John said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us."

R.38: John said to Jesus, "Teacher, we saw a man using {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to force demons to leave people. We told him to stop, because he was not one of our group."

decisions.choice: we were forbidding: we tried to stop him
decisions.reason: The imperfect can describe an attempt. It is not clear whether the man obeyed.

decisions.choice: in your name: calling on Jesus' name to drive out demons
decisions.reason: Exorcists used the names of powerful figures. Acts 19:13 tells of men who tried using the name of Jesus.

decisions.choice: following us: not one of the disciples' company
decisions.reason: John says "us", not "you". The concern is about belonging to their group.

decisions.choice: the wording of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: who does not follow us
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts add "who does not follow us" after "demons" and vary the order of the clauses. The meaning is not changed. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: throwing out (B); force to leave people (R)
decisions.reason: The pattern of earlier chapters.

records.heading: Whoever is not against us

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Μὴ κωλύετε αὐτόν, οὐδεὶς γάρ ἐστιν ὃς ποιήσει δύναμιν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ δυνήσεται ταχὺ κακολογῆσαί με·
records.gloss: But Jesus said, Not forbid him, no one for there is who will do a work of power in the name of me and will be able readily to speak evil of me;
pieces: Jesus said, "Do not stop him. No one who does a mighty work in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be quick to speak ill of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} afterward.

L.39: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a work of power in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and be able soon afterward to speak evil of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};

R.39: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him. A person who does a powerful miracle by using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will not soon turn around and say bad things about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: do not stop him: a present command, stop trying to prevent him
decisions.reason: The form tells them to give up what they were doing.

decisions.choice: soon afterward: quickly, readily
decisions.reason: The adverb means quickly. A man who has just done a mighty deed in Jesus' name will not turn at once to speak against him.

decisions.choice: work of power: a miracle
decisions.reason: The same word as in 6:2 and 6:5.

decisions.choice: will not soon turn around and say bad things about me
alternatives: will be able readily to speak evil of me
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the idiom.

records.source: ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθ’ ἡμῶν, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐστιν.
records.gloss: whoever for not is against us, for us is.
pieces: Anyone not against us is for us.

L.40: for whoever is not against us is for us.

R.40: If people are not against us, they are on our side.

decisions.choice: us, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "against you ... for you". The SBLGNT reads "us", which includes Jesus with his disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: not against us is for us: a generous rule for those who act in Jesus' name
decisions.reason: Matthew 12:30 gives the reverse: whoever is not with me is against me. There Jesus speaks of those who oppose him; here of one who acts in his name.

decisions.choice: on our side
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday phrase.

records.source: Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποτίσῃ ὑμᾶς ποτήριον ὕδατος ἐν ὀνόματι ὅτι χριστοῦ ἐστε, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Whoever for might give to drink you a cup of water in name that of Christ you are, truly I say to you that no not shall he lose the reward of him.
pieces: If anyone gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, truly I tell you, that person will certainly not lose the reward.

L.41: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in [the] name that you belong to the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, truly I say to you that {{gender:they|he}} will by no means lose {{gender:their|his}} reward.

R.41: I tell you the truth: if someone gives you so much as a cup of water because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, God will surely reward that person.

decisions.choice: in name that you are Christ's: because you belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase means on the ground that, or because. The gift is given to the disciples as Christ's people.

decisions.choice: Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed king
decisions.reason: Jesus rarely uses the title of himself in Mark. Peter has just confessed him as the Christ (8:29).

decisions.choice: in name that you are Christ's, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: in my name, because you are Christ's
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "in my name". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: his reward: the giver's reward from God
decisions.reason: Even the smallest kindness to Christ's people is seen and rewarded by God.

decisions.choice: so much as; God will surely reward
alternatives: will by no means lose the reward
decisions.reason: Readable says the promise positively and names God as the one who rewards. "So much as" brings out how small the gift is.

records.source: Καὶ ὃς ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, καλόν ἐστιν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον εἰ περίκειται μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ βέβληται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.
records.gloss: And whoever might cause to stumble one of the little ones these, the believing in me, better it is for him rather if is put a millstone of a donkey around the neck of him and he has been cast into the sea.
pieces: Whoever makes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fall away would be better off having a huge millstone hung around the neck and being thrown into the sea.

L.42: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stumble, it is better for {{gender:them|him}} if a donkey's millstone is put around {{gender:their|his}} neck and {{gender:they are|he is}} thrown into the sea.

R.42: Suppose someone leads one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into sin. It would be better for that person to have a heavy stone for grinding grain tied around the neck and be thrown into the sea.

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: cause to fall into sin or away from faith
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip someone up. In Mark it is used of falling away (4:17; 14:27).

decisions.choice: a donkey's millstone: the large upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey
decisions.reason: The word describes a millstone so heavy that an animal was needed to turn it. A man with one around his neck would sink at once.

decisions.choice: these little ones who believe in me: humble believers, like the child of 9:36
decisions.reason: "Little ones" follows the child Jesus held, but "who believe in me" shows that his followers are meant, however small.

decisions.choice: in me, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "in me". The SBLGNT includes it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: fall away (B); sin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling is.

decisions.choice: a heavy stone for grinding grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a millstone is.

records.heading: Better to enter life maimed

records.source: Καὶ ἐὰν σκανδαλίζῃ σε ἡ χείρ σου, ἀπόκοψον αὐτήν· καλόν ἐστίν σε κυλλὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν ἢ τὰς δύο χεῖρας ἔχοντα ἀπελθεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον.
records.gloss: And if causes to stumble you the hand of you, cut off it; better it is for you maimed to enter into the life than the two hands having to go away into the Gehenna, into the fire the unquenchable.
pieces: If your hand leads you into sin, cut it off. You are better off entering life maimed than going off with both hands into hell, into the fire that cannot be put out.

L.43: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than having two hands to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

R.43: If your hand makes you sin, cut it off. It is better to have only one hand and enter into life with God than to keep both hands and go to hell. Hell is the place where the fire never goes out.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the Valley of Hinnom, a name for the place of final judgment
decisions.reason: The Valley of Hinnom lay south of Jerusalem. Children had been burned there as sacrifices to idols (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31), and its name came to stand for the fire of God's judgment, as in Matthew 5:22.

decisions.choice: the unquenchable fire: fire that no one can put out
alternatives: a fire that burns for a while
decisions.reason: The fire of judgment cannot be stopped (Isaiah 66:24; Matthew 3:12).

decisions.choice: life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: "Life" here stands in parallel with "the kingdom of God" in 9:47.

decisions.choice: cut it off: get rid of whatever leads to sin, at any cost
decisions.reason: The picture is deliberately extreme. Losing a hand is better than losing everything.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 44
alternatives: add verse 44: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add here the words of 9:48, which also follow 9:45 in those manuscripts (verse 46). The earliest manuscripts lack them, and scribes likely copied the line from 9:48 to make the three sayings match. Verse 44 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, as in Matthew 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: life with God; Hell is the place where the fire never goes out
decisions.reason: Readable explains what life and hell mean here in short sentences.

records.source: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἀπόκοψον αὐτόν· καλόν ἐστίν σε εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν χωλὸν ἢ τοὺς δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν.
records.gloss: And if the foot of you causes to stumble you, cut off it; better it is for you to enter into the life lame than the two feet having to be cast into the Gehenna.
pieces: If your foot leads you into sin, cut it off. You are better off entering life lame than being thrown into hell with both feet.

L.45: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than having two feet to be thrown into Gehenna.

R.45: If your foot makes you sin, cut it off. It is better to be lame and enter into life with God than to keep both feet and be thrown into hell.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 46
alternatives: add verse 46: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
decisions.reason: As with verse 44, many later manuscripts repeat here the words of 9:48. The earliest manuscripts lack them, and they are likely a copy of 9:48. Verse 46 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: into Gehenna, the end of the saying in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "into the unquenchable fire", as in 9:43. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: to be thrown: a passive, the judgment of God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed. The one who judges is God.

decisions.choice: hell
decisions.reason: As in 9:43.

records.source: καὶ ἐὰν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζῃ σε, ἔκβαλε αὐτόν· καλόν σέ ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν, ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.
records.gloss: And if the eye of you causes to stumble you, cast out it; better for you it is one-eyed to enter into the kingdom of God than two eyes having to be cast into the Gehenna, \v 48 where the worm of them not dies and the fire not is quenched.
pieces: If your eye leads you into sin, tear it out. You are better off entering the kingdom of God with only one eye than being thrown into hell with two,
where the worm that eats them never dies and the fire is never put out.

L.47: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be thrown into Gehenna,
L.48: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.

R.47: If your eye makes you sin, take it out. It is better to have only one eye and enter the kingdom of God than to keep both eyes and be thrown into hell.
R.48: In that place the worms that eat people never die, and the fire never goes out.

decisions.choice: their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched: the last verse of Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah 66:24 describes the dead bodies of those who rebelled against God, eaten by worms and burned by fire that never ends.

decisions.choice: throw it out: the same verb as casting out demons
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the strong verb for driving out: get rid of it.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God: the same as life in 9:43 and 9:45
decisions.reason: The three sayings set "life" and "the kingdom of God" side by side as the same goal.

decisions.choice: their worm: the worm that feeds on those thrown there
alternatives: the worm that belongs to them as a pet
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the people in Gehenna.

decisions.choice: tear it out (B); take it out (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a verb that fits an eye. Literal keeps "throw out".

decisions.choice: hell
decisions.reason: As in 9:43.

records.source: Πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ἁλισθήσεται.
records.gloss: Everyone for with fire will be salted.
pieces: Everyone will be salted with fire.

L.49: For everyone will be salted with fire.

R.49: Every person will be salted with fire.

decisions.choice: everyone will be salted with fire, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: and every sacrifice will be salted with salt
every sacrifice will be salted with salt (in place of the saying)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and every sacrifice will be salted with salt", and some have that line instead. It comes from Leviticus 2:13, where every grain offering was to be seasoned with salt, and was likely added by scribes to explain the saying. The earliest manuscripts have only the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: salted with fire: everyone will be tested and purified, as a sacrifice is salted
alternatives: the wicked will be kept in the fire of judgment
disciples will be refined by suffering
decisions.reason: The saying is one of the hardest in Mark. "For" links it to the fire of 9:48. It may mean that every disciple will be made pure through trial, as offerings were salted (Leviticus 2:13). It may also mean that those in judgment are preserved in the fire. Mark does not explain it.

decisions.choice: for: the saying explains what came before
decisions.reason: The word ties the salt to the fire of the previous saying.

decisions.choice: Every person will be salted with fire
alternatives: everyone will be purified by fire
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture rather than choose one explanation, because the meaning is uncertain.

records.source: καλὸν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας ἄναλον γένηται, ἐν τίνι αὐτὸ ἀρτύσετε;
records.gloss: Good [is] the salt; if however the salt unsalty becomes, with what it will you season?
pieces: Salt is a good thing. But if the salt stops being salty, how will you give it back its flavor?

L.50: Salt [is] good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it?

R.50: Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, nothing can make it salty again.

decisions.choice: salt becomes unsalty: impure salt could lose its taste
decisions.reason: Salt gathered from the Dead Sea was mixed with other minerals. When the salt was washed out by damp, what was left looked like salt but had no taste.

decisions.choice: with what will you season it: a question expecting the answer, nothing
alternatives: a real request for a method
decisions.reason: Salt that has lost its taste cannot be restored.

decisions.choice: season: give it flavor
decisions.reason: The verb means to season food.

decisions.choice: nothing can make it salty again
alternatives: with what will you season it?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects.

records.source: ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἅλα, καὶ εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἀλλήλοις.
records.gloss: Have in yourselves salt, and be at peace with one another.
pieces: Have salt in yourselves, and live in peace with one another."

L.50: Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another."

R.50: Keep the salt in your lives, and live in peace with each other."

decisions.choice: in yourselves: within each of you, or among you as a group
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean in each person or among the company. With "one another" following, both may be in view.

decisions.choice: salt: the mark of a true disciple, perhaps also of a covenant shared
decisions.reason: Salt was part of God's covenant with Israel (Leviticus 2:13; Numbers 18:19), and sharing salt meant friendship. The call to be at peace answers the quarrel about greatness (9:34).

decisions.choice: be at peace: live in peace, the verb form of peace
decisions.reason: The verb is about relations between people.

decisions.choice: in your lives
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase that keeps the open sense.
